body_html:
[A10] Lane S1 for #665: the processor's other faces, census and contract 2.3. Executor [A680], reviewers [R701] (internal) and [R702] (external). Branch 665-s1-faces from dev-soft-core e76a755a; the PR targets dev-soft-core.

Problem. The split placement removes the whole KL_pp_shadow (ruling 6088423771, decision 1), but contract 2.2 carries only its class-D outputs (docs/design/MAILBOX_SPLIT.md:808-833). The datapath also reads its AECP settings, GET_COUNTERS, audio-map, #637 map-record, stream-info, enable and NVM faces (hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv:9359-9488, :9513-9641). MAILBOX_SPLIT.md:1036-1043 owes them to the placement switch, with no contract. This lane writes that contract. The placement switch (S6) connects it.

  1. Census, every port. Extend sw/mailbox/publication_census.py and census_rules.py, or add a sibling on census_elab.py, so the population is every port of the pp_shadow cell, in every shape the builder builds. Each port gets exactly one class:
    • C class-D, already in contract 2.2;
    • F firmware-written: aecp_cur_config_o, aecp_identify_o, aecp_clk_src_index_o, aecp_pt_offset_o/_v_o, aecp_fmt_in_o/_v_o, aecp_fmt_out_o/_v_o, aecp_dyn_dirty_o and aecp_lock_held_o (:9359-9370); one control-ready level in place of enable_i and restore_go_i (:9487-9488); the restore and NVM status levels the CSRs read;
    • R a request and answer window that keeps the datapath's answer logic unchanged: ctr_* (:9375-9385), amap_* read and edit (:9387-9408), gsi_* (:9428);
    • E an event record: ctr_change_*, gsi_avb_chg_i, gsi_asp_chg_i, amap_live_wr_i;
    • M a frame or event path that S6 connects: rx_*, m_axis_tx_*, link_up_i, gm_change_i, gm_id_i, gptp_domain_i;
    • G gone, tied to its reset value, with a reason: desc_mem_*, resp_mem_*, nvm_mem_*, nvm_csr_*, host_*, mrec_*, maap_* with cfg_maap_*, rx_frames_o/tx_frames_o/rx_drops_o, dbg_now_ms_o, and the static identity and configuration inputs.
      The census fails on an unmapped port, a port in two classes, and a G port whose consumer reaches the wire. It keeps its 31 rules and adds one per new rule, each with a plant and the standing rule-removal check. It runs in the existing publication-census job, at most 60 % of its timeout. No .github/ or CI-generator edit (#784).
  2. Contract 2.3 in sw/mailbox/mailbox.yaml, additive (minor). Per interface: the F registers, each with its width from the wrapper's port, and the R windows (request, index, busy/done, data) with a stated wait bound. New event types: COUNTERS_CHANGED (descriptor type and index), AVB_INFO_CHANGED, AS_PATH_CHANGED and AMAP_LIVE_WRITE, each with a coalescing rule that never loses the last state (MAILBOX_SPLIT.md:117-161). Every handshake and qualifying level must cross sys↔milan_cd through cdc_handshake or toggle-plus-sync (CONTRIBUTING.md:32-35): no multi-bit value is sampled without its qualifier. Regenerate KL_mbx*, mbx_contract.h and MAILBOX_CONTRACT.md. KL_mbx's new ports are named and left unread in CtrlMailbox (the sw/litex/milan_soc.py:2701-2712 pattern).
  3. Firmware. Implement aecp.h's platform ports changed, format, counters, stream and avb on contract 2.3, in sw/firmware/ctrl/aecp/ and app/. Rules:
    • each F value is written before the response that promises it (docs/ARCHITECTURE_HW_SW_SPLIT.md:55-57; Milan v1.2 5.4.5.2; IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.5.2);
    • COUNTERS_CHANGED drives the Table 5.22 notification, at most one per descriptor per second (Milan v1.2 Table 5.22);
    • every window read is bounded, and every new path's access count is added to the AECP bounds (sw/firmware/ctrl/aecp/README.md:202-210);
    • no synchronous port callbacks (#678); state per AVB interface;
    • the 100 % branch ratchet holds, with no new exclusion.
  4. Tests and plants.
    • RTL, in tb/verilator/mbx, through both adapters and run-if2: reset values, each field on its own port, the window handshake and its wait bound, out-of-window refusal, partial strobes, and event coalescing. Plants: a field on the wrong port, a window answering early, a dropped event, and a coalesced event that loses state.
    • Firmware, in GoogleTest: plants for a write after its response, a wrong field, a skipped write, a read past its bound and a missed change event, each killed by a named test.
  5. Unchanged. No milan_datapath.sv edit. No register-map change outside the mailbox block. The all-fabric export stays digest-identical for every shipped config (the method of MAILBOX_SPLIT.md:1138-1145). VERSION stays 0x0002_0060.
  6. Measure and report.
    • KL_mbx out of context (MAILBOX_SPLIT.md:1317-1329; Vivado under the host lock, queued behind the release builds), against 3,585 LUT, 4,114 FF, 1 RAMB36 and 10 RAMB18.
    • The linked image at 1x1 and 8x8, one and two interfaces (ctrl_srp_image.py --with-aecp --layout split), against 56 RAMB36 as mapped, with the delta from e76a755a and the five largest BSS consumers.

Gates (foreground, never piped, all rc 0):

  • make -C tb/verilator/mbx with run-if2 and mutants;
  • gen_mailbox.py --check --crosscheck --selftest;
  • the census --check --selftest;
  • test_ctrl_firmware.py --require-rv32 --self-test, fw_coverage.py --check and aecp_mutants.py;
  • test_builder.py --require-rv32, lint_rtl.py --check, xvlog_gate.py --check and syn/yosys/run.sh on the mailbox tops;
  • the docs gates.

STOP if:

  • a port fits no class above;
  • a face needs a datapath edit to classify;
  • the contract change is not additive;
  • any all-fabric export byte differs;
  • any of the four images exceeds 56 RAMB36;
  • a new CI job is needed;
  • an F value has no response it can be written before.

Post TAKEN, then REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head. Do not push.

body:
[A10] **S1 ruling on [A680]'s STOP (issuecomment-6410145305). Round 2: executor [A680b].**

1. **Decision 1: option (a).** `mrec_*`, `amap_unflushed_i` and `amap_alarm_i` stay in G.
   - The census names `amr_fsm`'s nets (`hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv:5456` and its restore and hold path, `:4824`, `:5448`, `:5520-5527`, `:5779-5794`) as removed with the wrapper. It stops a G cone there and lists that exclusion as owed to S6, by name.
   - S6's split datapath omits the map writer and restore. F5's owner applies the #637 restore (6009661573).
   - S6's split elaboration must then drop the exclusion, and the census must pass without it. Record that as an S6 acceptance item in the census's own text.
   - Option (b) is rejected: it would give map persistence two owners.
2. **Item 2: confirmed.** These are the three G-only terminals, each named by cell and port: `csr.i_pp_*` status inputs; the twenty memory-master outputs, listed one by one; and the `pp_maap_shim` cell, accepted only while each of its outputs reaches `pp_shadow` inputs alone. Every other end stays the wire. Each terminal gets a plant that moves a consumer past it, and the census must fail.
3. **Item 3: confirmed.** G with the stated reasons for `clk_i`, `rst_n`, `tx_drain_i`, `cfg_src_en_i`, `cfg_stream_id_i`, `cfg_tspec_max_frame_i`, `cfg_acc_lat_ns_i`, `port_rate_bps_i`, `amap_unflushed_i` and `amap_alarm_i`.
   - `cfg_stream_id_i` is shared with processor #202, which adds `src_stream_id_o` to the processor top (decision 6408987895).
   - Classify that new output when the pin adoption brings it. It will be class F or M, the published current Stream ID, and S6 wires the framer and GET_STREAM_INFO to the firmware's value.
4. **Interpretations: accepted.**
   - F restore and NVM status are written before AECP is released, and again on every change.
   - Add `AECP_CHANGE_LOCK` for `LOCK_HELD`.
   - One commit handshake per interface for the F block, with a bounded acknowledgement wait before the response.
5. **Census budget:** keep the new arms on the existing netlists. The hosted job stays at or under 60 % of its timeout (27 min). Record the measured time.

Build the design of the HANDOFF's "next round" section on these rulings. The assignment (6409739310) stands otherwise.

body:
[A10] **Owner clarification, 2026-10-26: the all-fabric placement stays a permanent, supported build choice.**

- **Class G** in the S1 census means "unused in the split build", not deleted: a generate branch with tie-offs. The all-fabric build instantiates `KL_pp_shadow`, the #637 map writer and restore (`amr_fsm`) and every face as today.
- **S6** omits those modules from the split build only. In the all-fabric build they stay, because there the fabric processor performs the #637 restore. S6's acceptance: both placements build from one tree and one key, and both pass their gates.
- **Every split-lane PR** keeps the all-fabric export byte-identical for every shipped config, as S1 item 5 says.
- **The flip (S13)** changes only the default and sets VERSION major 3. All-fabric remains buildable, and both placements keep their gates after the flip.

body:
[A10] **S1 ruling on [A680b]'s STOP (issuecomment-6412712270). Round 3: executor [A680c].**

1. **The budget at the largest point.** Owner decision D3 (6409738976) answers it: the firmware memory becomes a hybrid XIP, with cold code and the descriptor image in QSPI flash, in lane S14.
   - S1 is not blocked.
   - At **8x8 with two interfaces**, the image may plan **57** RAMB36. Record that point in `docs/design/SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md`'s ledger as over budget by 1 tile, owed to S14, by name, with this head's figures.
   - **Every other point** (1x1 one and two interfaces, 8x8 one interface) must stay within 56 RAMB36. STOP if any of them goes over.
   - The planner keeps refusing over-budget links by default. Add an explicit, named override for the one ledgered point, used only by that point's measurement; the default build path stays refusing. Add a test: the override does not apply to any other point.
   - The flip (S13) still requires 56 or fewer at every point, with S14 merged.
2. **The stack-protected runtime** (your measurement note): out of scope here. It is recorded for S3 (target platform firmware), which owns the runtime build for the target. Keep your one shared `-fno-stack-protector` runtime for the base and head figures, and state it in the PR body.
3. **Finish the gates you did not run:**
   - the whole firmware self-test, `test_builder.py --require-rv32`, `cd tests && behave`;
   - the four-shard sweep (memory rule);
   - the `KL_mbx` OOC run under the host lock, queued behind any release build;
   - the all-fabric export digest for every shipped config, which must be byte-identical (owner 2026-10-26: all-fabric stays a supported placement).
   Then post REVIEW READY.
